statement: A $4 \times 4$ grid has a lamp in each of its $16$ squares, and all the lamps start off. A move consists of choosing one row or one column and switching every lamp in it: a lamp that is off turns on, and a lamp that is on turns off. Any number of moves may be made, including none. Afterwards, Kim counts how many lamps are on. How many different counts are possible?

choices.misconception: I only switched rows, or only columns, so I found only the multiples of $4$: $0, 4, 8, 12, 16$.
I found $4, 6, 8, 10, 12$ and $16$ but forgot that $0$ lamps on is also possible, for example when no moves are made.
I saw that every count is even and assumed every even number from $0$ to $16$ is possible, including $2$ and $14$.
I assumed every number from $0$ to $16$ can be reached.

hints: Switching the same row twice undoes it, so all that matters is which rows and which columns are switched an odd number of times.
Say $r$ rows and $c$ columns are switched an odd number of times. A lamp is on exactly when its row or its column was switched, but not both. Count these lamps in terms of $r$ and $c$.
The number of lamps on is $r(4 - c) + c(4 - r) = 4r + 4c - 2rc$, where $r$ and $c$ can each be anything from $0$ to $4$. List the values.

solutions.reliable: Only whether each row and each column is switched an odd or even number of times matters. Say $r$ rows and $c$ columns are switched an odd number of times. A lamp is switched by its row and by its column, so it is on exactly when exactly one of the two was switched. That gives $r(4 - c) + c(4 - r) = 4r + 4c - 2rc$ lamps on. For $r = 0$ this is $4c$ and for $r = 4$ it is $16 - 4c$: the values $0, 4, 8, 12, 16$. For $r = 1$ it is $4 + 2c$ and for $r = 3$ it is $12 - 2c$: the values $4, 6, 8, 10, 12$. For $r = 2$ it is always $8$. Together the possible counts are $0, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16$, which is $7$ counts.
solutions.elegant: The count $4r + 4c - 2rc$ equals $8 - \frac{(4 - 2r)(4 - 2c)}{2}$. Each of $4 - 2r$ and $4 - 2c$ is one of $-4, -2, 0, 2, 4$, so their product is one of $0, \pm 4, \pm 8, \pm 16$. The count is therefore one of $8$, $8 \pm 2$, $8 \pm 4$, $8 \pm 8$, which are the $7$ values $0, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16$.
